messages:
From: Liam Carter <liam.carter@smallhealth.io>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Aug 2025 16:03:00 -0400
Subject: Private deploy pricing sensitivity + migration credit ask

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for the demo this morning — the team at SmallHealth liked the latency profile on medium-length clinical dialogues. Procurement asked me to get you a clearer ask: we need a short note that explains (1) how the platform fee is typically amortized across a 3-year on-prem deployment, (2) whether you can stage implementation credits tied to migration milestones, and (3) a few simple discount scenarios based on committed GPU node counts.

Attached: RFP v2 with our expected node mix and a spreadsheet with weekly query volume projections.

High level constraints: must keep data in our VPC (no traffic to hosted inference), and we have an internal limit on up-front CapEx this quarter — flexibility on amortization would help.

Can you send over 2–3 scenarios we can present to procurement by EOD tomorrow? Also — any exclusions on support SLA for academic research nodes?

—Liam
CTO, SmallHealth

Attachments: SmallHealth_RFP_v2.pdf (pdf), expected-node-metric.xlsx (xlsx)

Subject: Re: Private deploy pricing sensitivity + migration credit ask

Hi Liam — great meeting earlier. Looping in Aditya and Grace to get the full picture and concrete scenarios.

Quick ask for our internal team: can we put together three scenarios for SmallHealth by tomorrow morning:
- Scenario A (Conservative): 12-node reserved commit, 12-month amortization of platform fee, minimal implementation credit (one-time 10% of first-year platform fee)
- Scenario B (Balanced): 24-node commit, 24-month amortization, implementation credits staged at 25/50/25% across milestones (proof-of-concept, data migration, cutover)
- Scenario C (Aggressive): 36-node commit, 36-month amortization, larger upfront credit tied to multi-year commit + reduced support tier uplift

Customer note: they asked explicitly for staged credits tied to migration milestones and an avoidance of large up-front CapEx if possible. Also asked which support SLAs we exclude for academic/research-only nodes.

Aditya — can you confirm feasibility and any perf caveats for the expected node mix? Grace — can you sketch the discount math and whether we can convert some platform fee into a retainer-style on-call SKU to lower up-front numbers?

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: proposed-migration-milestones.docx (docx)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 19 Aug 2025 07:08:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy pricing sensitivity + migration credit ask

Hannah/Grace — scanned their spreadsheet. A few quick technical points that affect pricing options:

1) Node mix: they show a 2:1 ratio of RTX-class inference nodes to smaller CPU orchestration nodes. That implies steady-state unit cost will be dominated by GPU utilization; we should model effective token throughput not just node count.

2) KV/prefix caching: if they can permit a small shared KV cache during migration steps (still VPC-hosted), we can reduce peak node needs by ~15% — useful for the conservative scenario.

3) Support SLA: we can offer a research-only node class with a reduced SLA (best-effort debugging, 48-hour P1 response) but we must exclude it from Prod routing and the SLA must be explicit. This is an acceptable exclusion.

No blockers for staged credits — implementation credits can be billed as negative line items scheduled against invoices or delivered as professional-services hours covered by credits. For the staging, recommend milestone definitions tied to concrete deliverables (PoC sign-off, dataset transfer complete, production cutover) to avoid disputes.

I can draft simple wording for the SOW and milestone acceptance criteria if you want.

—Aditya
Principal Solutions Architect

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Private deploy pricing sensitivity + migration credit ask

Team — sketched scenarios below (rounded for email). I kept the math high-level so we can present to procurement quickly; if they want exact amort schedules we'll attach a spreadsheet.

Assumptions: platform fee baseline = $500k/year for the baseline deployment fabric (control plane + private management). GPU node annual run-rate per-node (incl infra mgmt) = $90k/node/year. Multi-year commits priced with standard volume ladder (5% @ 12, 10% @ 24, 15% @ 36 nodes) + contractual commit discounts.

Scenario A — Conservative- Commitment: 12 nodes- Annual platform fee amortization: 12 months (full first-year hit)- Implementation credit: 10% of first-year platform fee = $50k applied at cutover- Net first-year cash impact (platform + nodes, before any PS): platform $500k + nodes $1.08M = $1.58M; after credit = $1.53M

Scenario B — Balanced- Commitment: 24 nodes- Amortization: 24 months (spread platform fee over two years)- Implementation credits: 25% / 50% / 25% staged across milestones = $125k total- Discounting & ladder: effective node discount ~10% across commit = nodes $1.944M -> $1.75M- Net first-year cash: platform $250k (half amortized) + nodes $1.75M = $2.00M; after credits = $1.875M

Scenario C — Aggressive- Commitment: 36 nodes- Amortization: 36 months- Credits: larger upfront credit of 20% of first-year platform fee + 5% one-time account credit = ~$120k total- Node discounts: effective 15% -> nodes $2.754M -> $2.34M- Net first-year cash: platform $166k + nodes $2.34M = $2.506M; after credits = $2.386M

Operational note: to reduce up-front CapEx we can convert up to 50% of the platform fee into a retainer on a monthly on-call SKU (example: $250k/year retainer) — this reduces the up-front invoice by $250k but increases recurring Opex reporting. We can mark this as an optional line item for procurement.

Recommendation: present Scenario B as primary (balanced commit + staged credits) with Scenario A as a minimal fallback. Call out the research-node exclusion for SLA and make the milestone acceptance criteria explicit in the SOW.

If you want, I can attach a version of the amortization table and a draft SOW clause for milestone acceptance.

—Grace O'Connor
Head of Finance, Redwood Inference

Hannah/Aditya/Grace — thanks for the quick turn. This is helpful. A couple of follow-ups from procurement:

1) They want the staged credits expressed as either a negative invoice line or as PS hours; they prefer invoice credits. Can you confirm the mechanics?
2) For Scenario B, procurement asked whether the 24-node commit could be structured as a 12-node firm + 12-node optional (annual option to convert), with the same amortization and credits pro-rated. Would you be willing to price that?
3) For the research nodes: we will want a separate line item labelled "research cluster" with the reduced SLA and a clearly separated routing policy so we avoid accidental prod traffic.

If you can send a short bullet summary we can put in our internal proposal by EOD today, we should be ready to move to a formal commercial term sheet next week. Also open to a 30-min call tomorrow to walk procurement through the amortization math.

Best,
Liam
